r.name: D'Arcy Dalton Way
r.description: Follows roughly the western boundary of Oxfordshire in unspoilt countryside.

r.name: King Alfred's Way
r.description: King Alfreds Way is 350km (220 miles) off road route designed to be ridden clockwise. It starts & ends in Winchester. It is suitable for gravel or cross-country bikes.

r.name: The Vale Way
r.description: Route through the Vale of White Horse in Oxfordshire, UK. (27 miles).

r.name: Thames & Severn Way
r.description: Linking the Severn to the Thames following the route of the Stroudwater Navigation and Thames & Severn Canal as closely as possible using public rights of way. As the canals are restored, it will be updated to use the reinstated towpath wherever possible.

r.name: The Cole and its Landscape (Formerly the Red Walk: Coleshill)
r.description: Follow red way markers on this circular flat route through the Coleshill Estate. Some tracks and footpaths may be muddy and uneven, especially after rain. There are a number of stiles, gates and a small footbridge.

r.name: Ancient History & Agriculture Walk (Formerly the Orange Walk)
r.description: An undulating circular walk following farm tracks and footpaths across fields with an ascent through woodland. Some tracks and footpaths may be muddy and uneven.

r.name: White Horse Hill to Ashdown Walk, White Horse Hill
r.description: Long circular across the ancient chalk downs of Oxfordshire, neolithic sites and history found along this stretch of the ancient Ridgeway. Mixture of hard paths and field paths. Route can be muddy after wet weather. Take care at road crossings.

r.name: Parkland Walk, Coleshill
r.description: Short circular walk round the parkland at Coleshill

r.name: Faringdon Walk, Coleshill
r.description: Long circular hike from Faringdon to Great Coxwell and Coleshill. Mixed terrain and multiple stiles and gates on route.
